merger_description:
GForce 137 GmbH (**GForce**), which serves as the acquisition vehicle of SL510 S.à.r.l., a Luxembourg entity that is ultimately controlled by funds managed and advised by L Catterton Europe SAS, France (together with other affiliates, **L Catterton**), proposes to acquire 100% of the ordinary shares of HYROX World GmbH (**HYROX**) (the **Acquisition**).

Following the Acquisition, L Catterton and two of HYROX’s founders who will retain a stake in HYROX via the new holding structure, will hold joint control over HYROX.

GForce is a limited liability company under the laws of Germany, having its registered seat in Frankfurt am Main, Germany.

HYROX is a limited liability company incorporated and existing under the laws of Germany, registered with the commercial register of the local court of Hamburg. It is engaged in the business of organising, licensing, and operating indoor fitness racing events under the HYROX brand in several countries, including Australia.

L Catterton is a consumer-focused private equity group, whose portfolio companies operate across all segments of the consumer industry, including in the retail, restaurant, food and beverage, and consumer service and product businesses.

None of L Catterton’s portfolio companies are active in the same area of activity as HYROX in Australia, nor in an activity that is upstream or downstream of the organisation, licensing, and operation of indoor fitness racing events in Australia.

determination_table_content.details:
GForce 137 GmbH (GForce), the acquisition vehicle of SL510 S.à.r.l.,
which is ultimately controlled by funds managed and advised by L
Catterton Europe SAS, France (together with other affiliates, L
Catterton), applied for a notification waiver in respect of its
proposed acquisition of 100% of the ordinary shares of HYROX
World GmbH (HYROX), as described in the transaction documents
provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, L Catterton, is a consumer-focused private equity
group, whose portfolio companies operate across all segments of
the consumer industry, including in the retail, restaurant, food and
beverage, and consumer service and product businesses.
HYROX is a limited liability company incorporated and existing under
the laws of Germany, which is engaged in the business of organising,
licensing, and operating indoor fitness racing events under the
HYROX brand in several countries, including Australia.
None of L Catterton’s portfolio companies are active in the same
area of activity as HYROX in Australia, nor in an activity that is
upstream or downstream of the organisation, licensing, and
operation of indoor fitness racing events in Australia.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular, there is no horizontal overlap between the
operations of the parties or their connected entities in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
